in_window.name: Apple iOS 27 / macOS 27 'Golden Gate' accessibility (VoiceOver Image Explorer, Live Recognition, Coding verbosity tab)
in_window.category: OS-level AI accessibility
in_window.what_it_does: iOS 27 VoiceOver gains 'Image Explorer' (Apple Intelligence descriptions of photos, scanned bills, documents, on-screen graphics, with follow-up questions), 'Live Recognition' (camera + on-device models identify people/objects/surroundings in real time, invoked via Action button), a shareable/importable pronunciation dictionary, and an Accessibility Reader that handles tables/multi-column layouts. macOS 27 VoiceOver can describe and take questions about images or the whole screen via Apple Intelligence, adds a new 'Coding' verbosity tab (control announcement of line numbers, errors, warnings, breakpoints in editors such as Xcode), shows text-field labels in braille, and reintroduces several legacy voices.
in_window.date_or_version: Previewed May 19, 2026 (Apple Newsroom GAAD post); announced WWDC June 8, 2026; public release September 14, 2026 (iOS 27 / macOS 27). Dates come from multiple secondary snippets; primary Apple page could not be fetched.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: Mostly CONSUME (understanding images/documents/surroundings). The one explicit CREATE feature is the macOS VoiceOver 'Coding' verbosity tab, which AppleVis says is confirmed only for Xcode so far; Image Explorer also lets a blind creator check the images, charts and screenshots they themselves produce or publish.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Conversational follow-up on any image system-wide; a dedicated 'coding verbosity' profile (tones vs. spoken text for errors/breakpoints); user-controlled pronunciation dictionaries that can be exported and shared between devices and people.
in_window.gaps_left_open: AppleVis users report over-cautious 'sensitive content' refusals on ordinary images, vague person descriptions ('a person'), camera announcements interrupting descriptions, and the Coding tab's scope beyond Xcode is unknown; requires newer Apple Intelligence-capable hardware (sources conflict: iPhone 12+ vs iPhone 16+).

in_window.name: Google Gemini Live 'Guided Vision' + TalkBack 17.x / Android 17 accessibility updates
in_window.category: OS-level AI accessibility / voice assistant
in_window.what_it_does: Guided Vision is a camera-sharing mode in Gemini Live built for blind/low-vision users: continuous audio descriptions, verbal 'reframing' cues to point the camera correctly, follow-up questions while the camera stays live. Launchable from the TalkBack menu (three-finger tap), an Android accessibility shortcut, or Gemini settings; Android 9+ wherever Gemini Live is available. Google says 1,000+ members of Aira's Trusted Tester network stress-tested it and explicitly labels it 'not a medical device, mobility aid, or white cane replacement'. Separately, Android Accessibility Suite 17.1 / TalkBack 17.0 (Sept 29, 2026 build) adds more braille-display customization and better physical-keyboard support; Samsung's Android-17 One UI 9 (rolling out Oct 10, 2026) lets TalkBack update via the Play Store and adds Select to Speak. Google's I/O 2026 session covered Android 17 accessibility-API changes (Android 17 also restricts non-accessibility apps from the accessibility API in Advanced Protection mode).
in_window.date_or_version: Guided Vision announced in the September 2026 Android Drop (Sept 1, 2026, 'coming soon') and launched October 1, 2026 (blog.google); TalkBack 17.0 build Sept 29, 2026; One UI 9/Android 17 rollout Oct 10, 2026.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: CONSUME only (real-time scene/label/menu reading). Nothing in it targets building or publishing. Google's standalone Lookout app showed no 2026 update (Play listing last updated Aug 28, 2025); Guided Vision appears to be its successor inside Gemini.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: AI that takes responsibility for getting a usable camera shot (reframing cues) rather than making the blind user guess; co-development with a large blind tester network (Aira's 1,000+); explicit safety framing.
in_window.gaps_left_open: Hands-on reviewer (Accessible Android) found the TalkBack/shortcut entry points not yet live on their device and that a requested photo ended the session without confirmation; gradual rollout; no community-wide reaction threads found yet (launch was 11 days before this scan).

in_window.name: Research: computer-use agents for blind users ('Are We There Yet?', OLLA) and 'assistive agents need accessibility alignment'
in_window.category: Academic research (agents acting for blind users)
in_window.maker: Kodandaram, Reddy, Bi, Zhou, Ramakrishnan, Ashok (Stony Brook/ODU; EMNLP 2026); position paper authors (arXiv 2605.13579); Jakob Nielsen commentary
in_window.what_it_does: Three-week IRB diary study with 8 blind screen-reader users issuing 1,258 commands across 12 desktop apps through OLLA, a screen-reader-accessible computer-use agent prototype: GPT-5 52.5% success, Claude Sonnet 48.5%, Gemini 2.5 CU 43.9%, UI-TARS 39.8%, Qwen3-VL 37.9%; failures in grounding, planning, constraint tracking, termination (hallucinated controls, missed Save click). A CHI 2026 result cited by Nielsen: the same agent did 78% of tasks with a mouse but 42% keyboard-only. Position paper (May 2026) argues most agents are 'designed and evaluated under assumptions of sighted interaction'. Related 2026 preprints: 'Navigation Alone Is Not Enough' (Aug 2026) and 'Explainable AI for BLV users in the agentic era' (Apr 2026).
in_window.date_or_version: arXiv 2609.00524 submitted Sept 1, 2026 (EMNLP 2026 main); arXiv 2605.13579 May 2026; Nielsen UX Roundup Sept 25, 2026.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: Mixed: agents that operate GUIs on a blind user's behalf would unlock inaccessible CREATE tools (design apps, video editors), but success is ~50% and keyboard-only operation is much worse.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Screen-reader-native agent interface; interviews surfaced needs 'beyond automation' (explanation, confirmation before irreversible actions).
in_window.gaps_left_open: Half of tasks fail; no product ships this for blind users yet; evaluations assume sighted interaction.

verification.name: Research: computer-use agents for blind users ('Are We There Yet?', OLLA) and 'assistive agents need accessibility alignment'
verification.corrected_description: arXiv 2609.00524, 'Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users' Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications' (Kodandaram, Padma Reddy, Bi, Zhou, Ramakrishnan, Ashok), submitted Sept 1, 2026 and accepted to EMNLP 2026 Main, is confirmed: three-week diary study, 8 blind users, OLLA accessibility layer over existing CUAs, 1,258 commands across 12 applications, GPT-5 best at 52.5%, four additional models re-executed, failures in grounding/planning/constraint tracking/termination, interviews on 'beyond-automation' needs. 'Navigation Alone Is Not Enough' (arXiv 2608.09944) also appears in results. Not verified: the exact success rates for Claude Sonnet/Gemini/UI-TARS/Qwen3-VL, the May 2026 position paper 2605.13579, the CHI 2026 78%-vs-42% keyboard figure, and the Nielsen Sept 25, 2026 roundup.
verification.corrected_date: September 1, 2026 (arXiv submission; EMNLP 2026 main)
verification.verdict_reason: arXiv abstract snippet confirms the paper, authors, date, venue, study size and headline result; the ancillary papers and commentary are partly or wholly unverified.

Analysis of development logs and feedback identifies BLV strategies for tool creation and key challenges: model capability limits, specification conflicts, and barriers to successful creation; success 'rarely comes from a single prompt' but from iterative testing and debugging reports (third-party review).

in_window.name: 'Characterizing Visual Accessibility Issues in AI Developer Tools: An Empirical Study' (600 mined reports across Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode)
in_window.category: Research (preprint) on accessibility bug reports in AI coding tools
in_window.what_it_does: Mined public issue trackers and forums of five AI developer-tool ecosystems (GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode) for visual-accessibility reports: 2,652 keyword candidates filtered by a three-model LLM ensemble to 600 reports confirmed by manual sampling. Topic modeling and qualitative coding yield three recurring categories: screen-reader/assistive-technology barriers; visual presentation, contrast and differentiation problems; readability, scaling and control limits in AI-specific interfaces. The mix tracks each tool's interaction surface (editor, terminal, chat, diff, agent). Exploratory metadata analysis finds differences in reporter activity, maintainer participation and how issues are closed across the GitHub-based tools.
in_window.date_or_version: arXiv preprint, ~5 Aug 2026 (v1)
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: Quantifies, across all the major vibe-coding tools, what blind and low-vision users report breaking, and documents the maintainer-response disparity that this scan also observed anecdotally.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: The taxonomy (AT barriers / presentation / scaling-control) as an audit checklist for any new builder tool; tracking maintainer participation and closure type as an accessibility metric.
in_window.gaps_left_open: Describes reported barriers, not measured prevalence; relies on LLM classification; no peer-reviewed venue yet; full text not readable through the proxy.

in_window.name: OLLA / 'Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users' Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications' (EMNLP 2026)
in_window.category: Research on AI agents operating software for blind users
in_window.what_it_does: OLLA is a screen-reader-accessible shell around computer-use agents for desktop applications. A diary-style study with 8 blind users collected 1,258 natural-language commands across 12 desktop applications; the best model (GPT-5) completed 52.5% successfully. Jakob Nielsen's UX Roundup (25 Sep 2026) discusses the result and a related finding that an agent completed 42% of tasks when restricted to keyboard-only interaction versus 78% with a mouse.

in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: Shows the 'tell the AI to do this for me' use case the user described is only about half-reliable today for desktop GUIs, and that keyboard-only operation (what blind users need) is markedly worse than mouse-driven agents.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Wrapping agents in a screen-reader-native command shell; measuring success specifically under keyboard-only constraints.
in_window.gaps_left_open: 52.5% success is far from dependable; arXiv blocked so figures come from snippets; not specific to coding tools.

in_window.name: Characterizing Visual Accessibility Issues in AI Developer Tools: An Empirical Study
in_window.category: Research preprint — empirical mining of accessibility bug reports in AI coding tools
in_window.maker: Sabrina Haque, Christoph Csallner (University of Texas at Arlington)
in_window.what_it_does: Mined public issues and forum posts from five AI developer tools — GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and OpenCode. From 2,652 keyword-matched candidates, a three-model ensemble plus stratified manual checking kept 600 confirmed visual-accessibility reports. Topic modeling + qualitative coding yielded three categories: (1) screen-reader/assistive-technology barriers, (2) visual presentation/contrast/differentiation problems, (3) readability, scaling and control limitations specific to AI interfaces. Category prominence varied by tool, tracking differences between editor, terminal, chat, diff and agent interfaces; maintainer engagement and issue-closure patterns differed across the GitHub-based tools.
in_window.date_or_version: arXiv 2608.05116, submitted 5 August 2026 (v1)
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: First systematic map of where the current 'vibe coding' stack breaks for blind/low-vision/CVD developers, by tool and by interface surface (terminal agents vs chat vs diff views). Tells a product team exactly which surfaces are the pain points to design around.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Issue taxonomy as an acceptance-test checklist for any new coding surface; the finding that agent/terminal interfaces have their own distinct accessibility failure profile argues for a dedicated screen-reader-first agent console.
in_window.gaps_left_open: Authors call the selection conservative and the metadata analysis exploratory; per-tool counts not retrieved; no user study — only what people bothered to report publicly.

in_window.name: Coral: Contextual Gists for Blind and Low Vision Screen Reader Users' Understanding of Dynamic User Interfaces

in_window.maker: Ritesh Kanchi, Jianna So, Krzysztof Z. Gajos (Gajos is at Harvard — affiliation inferred, not verified)
in_window.what_it_does: Interviewed 11 BLV screen-reader users about how they understand dynamic UIs, then built Coral, a context-aware Chromium browser extension (TypeScript/React) that fuses interface context (structural, semantic, visual evidence) with user context (recent interactions, prior states) to generate short 'gists' describing what changed, where, and how it relates to recent activity. in_window.date_or_version: arXiv 2609.22799 v1, September 2026 (cs.HC)

in_window.name: "I'm Always a Little Skeptical of It": Verification Practices of Blind Users When Working with Generative AI in Spreadsheets
in_window.category: Research paper — how blind users verify AI output in data work (CHI 2026)
in_window.maker: Minoli Perera, Swamy Ananthanarayan, Cagatay Goncu, Kim Marriott (Monash University)
in_window.what_it_does: Remote study with 12 blind spreadsheet users doing four GenAI-assisted task types — information extraction, formula generation, chart creation, and formatting. Participants never fully trusted outputs without checking. Strategies: manual inspection with screen reader + spreadsheet features (most started here), using a second AI to verify or describe the first AI's output, comparing across AI tools, relying on prior knowledge, and asking humans. Verification cost more time and effort for visually intensive tasks (chart generation, formatting), and some errors slipped through (e.g., an incorrect minimum-value entry went unnoticed). Authors argue GenAI 'shifts responsibility onto the user'.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: Blind people doing data analysis with AI can produce charts and formulas they cannot see; this paper documents the verification labor that lands on them and where it fails. Any product that lets blind people build (charts, UIs, documents) must budget for non-visual verification.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Built-in 'second opinion' AI describing the visual result; structured non-visual summaries of layout/formatting after each AI edit; error-prone task classes (charts, formatting) flagged for mandatory review.
in_window.gaps_left_open: 12 participants, spreadsheet-only; no tool proposed; does not measure how much verification actually catches.

verification.name: "I'm Always a Little Skeptical of It": Verification Practices of Blind Users When Working with Generative AI in Spreadsheets

in_window.name: Chart-Supported or Model-Supplied? Examining MLLM-Generated Claims for Accessible Visualization
in_window.category: Research preprint — hallucination/attribution audit of AI chart descriptions (AccessViz workshop @ IEEE VIS 2026)
in_window.maker: Ishrat Jahan Eliza, Md Dilshadur Rahman (institution not confirmed)
in_window.what_it_does: Exploratory study of 102 visualizations from four sources, three MLLMs, four input conditions (varying image access, accessible chart context, and a withheld-context prompt); 1,224 generated descriptions. Models tagged each claim DIRECT / DERIVED / SPECULATIVE and the authors audited numeric agreement. Accessible chart context shifted Gemini and GPT toward DIRECT claims and improved numeric agreement for some models; adding the image to full context gave no consistent numeric benefit; the withheld-context prompt did not reliably increase cautious wording; 'Real-World Significance' sections stayed mostly SPECULATIVE even with the richest inputs.
in_window.date_or_version: arXiv 2607.25021, submitted 27 July 2026 (v2 later); submitted to the 3rd Workshop on Accessible Data Visualization, IEEE VIS 2026
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: When a blind person asks an LLM to describe (or verify) a chart they just generated, this paper shows which parts of the answer are grounded and which are made up. Supports a product design that labels every claim as chart-supported vs model-supplied.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Claim-level provenance tags (DIRECT/DERIVED/SPECULATIVE) in descriptions; feeding structured chart context (data/spec) rather than only the image; separate 'interpretation' section clearly marked as model opinion.
in_window.gaps_left_open: Workshop-stage; no blind-user study; model versions will drift.

Authors: Monalika Padma Reddy, Aruna Balasubramanian, Jiawei Zhou, Xiaojun Bi, IV Ramakrishnan and Vikas Ashok (Stony Brook / Old Dominion). CHI '26, Barcelona, 13-17 April 2026, Article 1247, DOI 10.1145/3772318.3790955; arXiv preprint 2602.18630 posted 20 Feb 2026. Interview study plus usability study with blind participants on using product manuals and AI tools for physical DIY tasks. Key finding is more negative than the scout implies: manuals often fall short and AI tools 'often exacerbate this issue with incomplete, incoherent, or misleading guidance', e.g. bundling several actions into one step.

in_window.name: MCP specification 2026-07-28, MCP Apps, and accessibility-related MCP registry servers

in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: MCP is the plumbing a voice/keyboard-first builder platform would use to give an agent tools; the registry already contains accessibility auditors an agent can call while generating UI, and MCP Apps is the route for non-visual interactive widgets.

verification.corrected_description: MCP spec 2026-07-28 RC was released May 29, 2026 and the stable revision July 28, 2026. Its changelog confirms: protocol-level sessions, Mcp-Session-Id and the initialize handshake removed (version/capabilities carried in _meta); required `server/discover`; `subscriptions/listen` replaces HTTP GET stream and resources/subscribe; Multi Round-Trip Requests (`input_required` results) replace server-initiated roots/list, sampling and elicitation; tasks moved to the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension; resumability (Last-Event-ID) removed. in_window.name: Claude Code screen reader mode (--ax-screen-reader), desktop and VS Code accessibility fixes
in_window.category: AI coding agent (CREATE tool)
in_window.what_it_does: An opt-in mode that turns the Claude Code terminal UI into plain, sequential text for screen readers: 'you:/claude:/tool:' labels, numbered menus answered by typing a number + Enter, y/n prompts, spinners and box-drawing removed, terminal bell on reply completion/permission prompt/long tool finish, OSC 133 prompt markers. Enabled by `claude --ax-screen-reader`, `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1`, or `"axScreenReader": true` in ~/.claude/settings.json (needs v2.1.181+; v2.1.206+ announces '[Screen Reader Mode: on via flag]'). Separately, Claude Code desktop v1.17377 (July 21, 2026) added per-turn headings, ARIA landmarks, announced permission requests and response start/end for NVDA on Windows; the VS Code extension v2.1.236 (Aug 20, 2026) added live announcements and per-turn heading navigation for JAWS.
in_window.date_or_version: Mode shipped on 'latest' channel v2.1.181 (announced July 1, 2026), official release + support article July 13-20, 2026; issue #11002 closed as completed July 21, 2026; desktop fixes v1.17377 July 21, 2026; VS Code fix v2.1.236 Aug 20, 2026.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: CREATE. This is the most-cited tool in blind vibe-coding accounts of 2026 (AFB AccessWorld, Double Tap, Tim Dixon, NFB seminar). The mode exists because blind developers filed detailed issues since Nov 2025.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Linear-text mode as a first-class switch; numbered menus; bell/earcon on 'needs input'; per-turn headings so screen reader users can jump between prompts and replies; announce permission requests without stealing focus (so a reflexive Enter can't grant a persistent permission).
in_window.gaps_left_open: Verified from the issues: no built-in spoken status/TTS or 'humanized' tool-name announcements; input line re-renders per keystroke; bell cannot be disabled in this mode; some panels lack hardware-cursor support; the mode does not reach the VS Code webview; Claude Desktop/claude.ai virtualizes the chat list to ~10 messages making long conversations unstable for JAWS/NVDA (#83167, auto-closed 'not planned' Sept 9, 2026 with no maintainer reply); #70425 umbrella request auto-closed as stale Sept 19, 2026; Alt+Tab unresponsive with NVDA reported Sept 16, 2026 with no reply.

in_window.name: Claude Code CLI screen reader mode (--ax-screen-reader / CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER / axScreenReader)
in_window.category: Dedicated accessibility feature in an AI coding agent (terminal)
in_window.what_it_does: Opt-in mode that replaces Claude Code's visual TUI with plain linear text: no box-drawing, no color-only cues, no redraws of unchanged content, spinners rendered as static text, tables read as 'Header: value' sentences, diffs read line by line with +/- so a permission prompt can be heard before answering. Every transcript message gets a searchable label (you:, claude:, thinking:, tool:, tool error:, error:, warning:, Permission Required:, Cost:). Arrow-key menus (including permission prompts and the /effort slider) become numbered lists answered by typing a number; yes/no prompts take y/n. Terminal bell rings when a reply finishes, a prompt needs an answer, or a tool running >5 s finishes. Emits OSC 133 markers so iTerm2/VS Code/Windows Terminal jump-to-prompt keys move between turns. Announces deleted words/lines and permission-mode changes via Shift+Tab. Confirmation line '[Screen Reader Mode: on via flag|env|settings]' then a 3 s quiet period (CLAUDE_AX_STARTUP_QUIET_MS, v2.1.217+). CLAUDE_AX_PREPARK_MS (v2.1.233+). Separate CLAUDE_CODE_ACCESSIBILITY=1 keeps the cursor visible for magnifiers (follows menu rows from v2.1.218). prefersReducedMotion and dark/light-daltonized themes. Docs say it does NOT auto-enable when a screen reader is running, costs are only announced at exit, attached background sessions use the alternate screen with no scrollback, and -p headless mode is unchanged.
in_window.date_or_version: Changelog entry 'Added screen reader mode' in v2.1.208 (14 Jul 2026). Earlier related entries: v2.1.200 (3 Jul 2026) 'Improved screen-reader output: decorative glyphs hidden, transcript symbols read as short labels, nested tables read as Header: value lines' and 'Fixed /mcp server list not tracking focus for screen readers and magnifiers'. Anthropic support article dated 13 Jul 2026 says the mode requires v2.1.181 or later (v2.1.181 released 17 Jun 2026; its release page shows no a11y entry, so the exact first version is unresolved). Public announcement on X by @ClaudeDevs 20 Jul 2026. Later refinements: v2.1.288 (plan-approval permission-mode announcement, short announcements persist until next key, 'answered' marker in question dialogs), v2.1.290, v2.1.295 (VS Code reduced-motion fix) in Oct 2026.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: This is the first terminal coding agent with a fully documented screen-reader mode, and the terminal is where blind developers already live (AppleVis thread 'Terminal-Based Linux as a Practical Platform for Blind Programmers'). It makes the whole agent loop (prompt, permission approval, hearing the diff, reading output) operable with NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver, which is the precondition for a blind person to build an app, site or research tool with Claude Code rather than only chat about it.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Labeled, searchable transcript lines (you:/claude:/tool:); numbered-list menus instead of arrow navigation; hear-the-diff-before-approving; bell on turn end/prompt/long tool; OSC 133 turn markers; announcing deleted text and mode changes; explicit documentation of limitations and of the NVDA+6 review-cursor trick; a startup quiet period so the confirmation line is not talked over.
in_window.gaps_left_open: Not auto-detected (issue #89002 asks for SPI_GETSCREENREADER-style detection); still verbose in places (VoiceOver box-drawing runs, #91058; slash-menu arrow keys silent, #100253; AskUserQuestion picker unusable with NVDA, #88839; manual-mode diff not shown, #98706); no built-in TTS, earcons or heading discipline (maintainer confirmed not shipped, #70425); env-var activation reportedly failed on Linux v2.1.237 (#88221, closed by bot without reply); costs not announced per turn; attached background sessions lose scrollback. Version documentation is inconsistent (2.1.181 vs 2.1.208).

in_window.name: Claude Desktop app (Code and Chat tabs) screen reader bugs and the community 'stable-feed' workaround

in_window.maker: Anthropic (app); workaround by GitHub user thyhellcat (blind JAWS user)
in_window.what_it_does: Blind JAWS/NVDA/VoiceOver users report the Claude Desktop transcript is a virtualized list: ampage87 (#83167, 1 Aug 2026) measured a fixed window of 10 rendered messages regardless of viewport, with unrendered history replaced by an aria-hidden spacer, so messages vanish from the virtual buffer mid-read; closed by stale bot 9 Sep. thyhellcat (#99332, 3 Oct 2026) found the root cause (rows outside the visible height + 600 px margin are unmounted; keepMountedRef protects only focused/selected/pinned rows, not the screen reader's reading cursor; in one session 'only 4 rows out of 116 were in the DOM') and published claude-desktop-stable-feed, a DevTools console script that makes the scroller report a huge clientHeight so every row stays mounted and moves focus to the last message on session switch; must be re-run each launch. Other desktop reports in window: #87977 (19 Aug, macOS VoiceOver cursor jumps, sidebar hard to navigate), #94353 (14 Sep, Windows: slash command menu in Code tab silent for NVDA), #95937 (21 Sep, Windows: new replies in Code tab not announced by NVDA), #99818 (6 Oct, plugin labels read twice by VoiceOver), #100911 (9 Oct, Mac: every line of the file/diff panel announced as 'Add comment', code never read - rated Blocker), #91606 (2 Sep, unlabeled tray icon), #82288/#82289 (29 Jul, Windows dialogs render off-screen; closed by bot). in_window.name: CHI 2026 paper: 'Programmers Who Use Screen Readers in the Vibe Coding Era: Adaptation, Empowerment, and New Accessibility Landscape'
in_window.category: Research (peer-reviewed) on blind developers using AI coding assistants
in_window.maker: Nan Chen, Luna K. Qiu, Arran Zeyu Wang, Zilong Wang, Yuqing Yang (Microsoft Research Asia)
in_window.what_it_does: Three-phase longitudinal study with 16 blind and low-vision programmers using GitHub Copilot in VS Code (tutorial + task + feedback, then two weeks of use, then follow-up). Findings: assistants 'enhanced programming efficiency and bridged accessibility gaps' (participants took on UI work they had avoided; natural-language undo), but participants 'struggled to convey intent, interpret AI outputs, and manage multiple views while maintaining situational awareness'; preferences for accessibility features varied; tension between automation and control; learning barriers. Eight design recommendations in four areas (predictable shortcuts and clarification of vague prompts; clear change indicators, grouped messages, full-detail accessible view, optional autoplay; a consolidated single panel; separating AI-driven actions from ones needing input plus a 'Do Not Disturb' setting), and calls for screen-reader-first learning materials and per-user personalization.
in_window.date_or_version: CHI '26 Article 1198, published 13 Apr 2026 (DOI 10.1145/3772318.3790726); arXiv preprint 2506.13270 (Jun 2025); Microsoft Research summary article 29 Sep 2025 (pre-window)
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: The most rigorous evidence in the window that AI assistants expand what blind programmers can build (UI work in particular) and a precise list of what still blocks them (orientation across editor/chat/terminal, vague status, linear message navigation).
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Single consolidated panel with self-verification; grouping related messages under headings/indexes; optional autoplay of long responses; sound or text change indicators; 'Do Not Disturb'; clarifying questions for vague prompts; learning materials written for screen reader users.
in_window.gaps_left_open: Studied Copilot only, in 2025, before agent modes matured; participants were existing programmers, not non-developers; its recommendations are only partly implemented by any vendor as of Oct 2026.

in_window.what_it_does: Three-phase longitudinal study with 16 blind and low-vision programmers: GitHub Copilot tutorial + programming task + initial feedback, then two weeks of AI-assisted programming, then follow-up interviews on how practices and perceptions evolved. in_window.gaps_left_open: Studied Copilot (completion/chat era), not fully autonomous agents; no tooling built, only principles; longer-term skill effects unknown.

in_window.name: Claude Code screen reader mode (and voice dictation)
in_window.category: AI coding agent / terminal accessibility
in_window.what_it_does: Opt-in plain-text rendering of the Claude Code CLI for screen readers: `claude --ax-screen-reader`, `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1`, or `"axScreenReader": true`. No box-drawing chrome, no color-only cues, static spinners, tables read as `Header: value`, diffs read line by line with +/-, every transcript message prefixed with a searchable label (you:/claude:/thinking:/tool:/error:/Permission Required:), numbered menus instead of arrow-key menus (type a number), y/n prompts, terminal bell when a reply finishes or a prompt waits, OSC 133 markers so terminals can jump between turns, announcements of deleted words/lines and of permission-mode changes. Related: `/voice` push-to-talk dictation (hold or tap Space; transcription on Anthropic servers, needs a claude.ai login, not in SSH/cloud sessions) and a VS Code extension that announces replies, permission requests, errors and status changes, with per-turn heading navigation.
in_window.date_or_version: Screen reader mode added in v2.1.208, published to npm 2026-07-13. Follow-ups: v2.1.210 (2026-07-14) permission-mode announcements; v2.1.217/218 (2026-07-21/22) startup announcement, deleted-text announcements, VoiceOver space echo; v2.1.219/222 (Jul 24/Aug 4) per-keystroke echo fixes; v2.1.233 (Aug 14) /effort as numbered list; v2.1.236 (Aug 19) VS Code transcript screen-reader support; v2.1.268/269/274 (Sep 10-16) VS Code keyboard/screen-reader commands; v2.1.281-283 (Sep 23-25) list/diff/quoted-command fixes; v2.1.287/288 (Oct 1-2) cursor placement, diff lines in approvals, plan-approval announcement; v2.1.290 (Oct 5) 'Message queued' announcement. `/voice` dictation predates the window (changelog entries from v2.1.69, 2026-03-04).
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: This is the single most concrete in-window change for 'vibe coding' without sight: a mainstream coding agent now has a documented, linear, screen-reader-first interface, plus voice input. Blind developers in the window used it to build game mods, apps and tools (see other items). The docs page itself is a model for how to specify a non-visual interface.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Labelled, searchable transcript lines; numbered-choice menus with a spoken valid range; bell on turn-end/prompt/long tool; 'write only the characters that changed' input echo; announce deletions and mode changes once (no re-announce on redraw); configurable quiet period at startup (CLAUDE_AX_STARTUP_QUIET_MS); OSC 133 turn markers; a separate 'magnifier cursor' setting (CLAUDE_CODE_ACCESSIBILITY) and reduced-motion/daltonized themes decoupled from screen-reader mode; voice push-to-talk with coding-vocabulary hints (project and branch names).
in_window.gaps_left_open: Does not auto-enable when a screen reader is running (documented limitation; issues #89002, #87978); startup 3-5 s slower in screen-reader mode (#99188, Oct 3); streaming output still read live, no 'hold speech until the turn ends' option (#87978; a community plugin adds it); attached background sessions use the alternate screen with no scrollback; VoiceOver still reads box-drawing runs in some views (#91058); NVDA cannot select text in the prompt (#92287); /voice live transcript stalls on Windows (#96440); voice needs a claude.ai account and local mic, so no dictation over SSH or in cloud sessions.

in_window.name: Blind-built accessibility layers for Claude Code: accessible-claude-code (x2), claude-code-earshot, skills-for-the-blind
in_window.category: Community tooling around AI coding agents
in_window.maker: digitalby; joseph-webber (self-described blind developer); Unlocked Spark Foundation; Engccer (self-described blind author, Korea)
in_window.what_it_does: digitalby/accessible-claude-code (created 2026-04-13): a PTY wrapper that makes Ink-based TUIs such as Claude Code usable with VoiceOver/NVDA/Narrator by filtering spinner repaints. joseph-webber/accessible-claude-code (created 2026-07-16; README says 'v0.1 — early but functional (June 2026)'): a harness that runs Claude Code as a local process in the Mac GUI session and exposes it to thin screen-reader-perfect web/iOS/CLI clients with voice. unlocked-spark/claude-code-earshot (created 2026-10-10; needs Claude Code 2.1.292+): a Claude Code plugin that detects NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver, offers to switch screen-reader mode on, delivers each answer whole instead of streaming, speaks 'Starting work.' and 'Still working, 10 seconds.', hides tool noise with /earshot-tools brief|full, and localizes to six languages. Engccer/skills-for-the-blind (created 2026-07-07): a Korean-first bundle of five agent skills (docparse, hwpx-automation, abridge, agent-cli-tts-summary, speech-toolkit) so a blind screen-reader user can read, condense, hear and dictate when working with Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: Shows blind developers filling the gaps vendors leave within weeks: the April wrapper predates Anthropic's July screen-reader mode, and the October plugin fixes exactly the complaints in issue #87978 (whole-answer delivery, turn-start/heartbeat speech, auto-detection). The Korean bundle shows the full creator loop (documents in, speech out, voice in) being assembled from skills.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Screen-reader detection at startup with a one-question opt-in; whole-answer delivery with a bell; periodic 'still working' heartbeat; tool-call narration levels (off/brief/full) plus /earshot-last to replay a result; install path that avoids an inaccessible picker; skills as the packaging unit for accessibility workflows; a 'field notes' repo of spec-compliant patterns that still fail on real screen readers.
in_window.gaps_left_open: All are single-maintainer projects with 0-1 stars; earshot cannot run under WSL, `claude -p`, the SDK, the VS Code panel or the cloud; joseph-webber's client is macOS-only v0.1; the Korean bundle targets Korean document formats (HWPX).

Blog series Aug 6-Sep 28, 2026 documents the build with both sides of the agent conversations quoted; 'An hour a day' (Aug 30) measures 131 merged PRs / 193 commits in seven weeks, 84.2 hours of which 70% was the machine working and ~1 hour per active day was his own attention. in_window.name: Robert Kingett: 'The Disability Dongle' and 'A Thermodynamic Failure of the Soul' - blind writer's warnings about inspiration porn, technoableism and AI framing
in_window.category: Community voice - critique/warning
in_window.maker: Robert Kingett (blind writer, critic, editor; blog mirrored on GitHub rkingett/myblog)
in_window.what_it_does: Aug 5, 2026 post: names 'The Inspiration Porn Industrial Complex' (college team, piano soundtrack, $30,000 stair-climbing wheelchair) and the 'Disability Dongle' - 'engineering designed for the abled gaze, not the disabled body'; says smart-glasses and haptic belts are 'costumes'; 'Silicon Valley will spend millions developing a glove that translates sign language into speech (badly), but they won't spend ten minutes adding Alt-Text'; ends 'Just fix your fucking code. Pour some concrete. And stop trying to upgrade my body when the problem is your design.' Aug 18, 2026 post: a writer friend assumed his human editing was done by an LLM; he notes 'While many in the blind community use LLMs unapologetically and proudly, I know people who do not enjoy using these disability dongles but they continue to use these large language models out of sheer, grinding necessity. I know blind peers who code software through an LLM because ableist developers refuse to code structural accessibility into their applications... The tech industry treats this disabled survival as free marketing.'
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: The strongest in-window warning against the 'AI superpowers for blind people' marketing frame: blind people coding through LLMs is partly a response to inaccessible software, and treating it as a savior story is exploitation. Any product must avoid the savior/inspiration posture.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Fix the code first (semantic HTML, labels, headings); honor low-tech robustness ('my white cane... has no batteries. It never crashes'); never market disabled users' necessity as inspiration.
in_window.gaps_left_open: No product fixes this; it is a stance. He also links mosen.org/ai as an example of blind people using LLMs 'unapologetically and proudly' (not fetched).

in_window.name: Claude Code screen reader mode (CLI)
in_window.category: AI coding agent / accessibility mode
in_window.what_it_does: Opt-in plain-text rendering for the Claude Code terminal UI: `claude --ax-screen-reader`, `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1`, or `"axScreenReader": true`. Replaces boxes, spinners and in-place redraws with labeled linear lines (`you:`, `claude:`, `thinking:`, `tool:`, `Permission Required:`), numbered-list menus answered by typing a number, y/n prompts, plain-text diffs with +/- lines, terminal bell when Claude finishes or needs input, OSC 133 turn markers for jump-to-prompt, announcements of deleted words/lines and of permission-mode changes (Shift+Tab). Also `CLAUDE_CODE_ACCESSIBILITY=1` (visible cursor for magnifiers), `prefersReducedMotion`, daltonized themes.
in_window.date_or_version: Added in v2.1.208 (npm published 2026-07-13); featured in Claude Code 'Week 29 · July 13–17, 2026' digest. Continuous fixes through v2.1.290 (2026-10-05), e.g. 2.1.218 (Jul 22) deletion announcements, 2.1.233 (Aug 14) /effort as numbered list, 2.1.287–2.1.288 (Oct 1–2) diff and search-box fixes.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: First mainstream coding agent with a documented, maintained non-visual mode; makes end-to-end building (approve permissions, hear diffs, run tools) possible from a terminal with NVDA/VoiceOver. Community issue #11002 (66 comments, opened Nov 2025) requested exactly this.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Labeled line prefixes that double as search anchors; numbered menus instead of arrow-key selection; bell/earcon on 'needs you'; announce only changed characters when typing; startup quiet period (CLAUDE_AX_STARTUP_QUIET_MS); OSC 133 turn markers so the terminal's own jump keys navigate turns.
in_window.gaps_left_open: Mode is not auto-detected; no built-in spoken status/TTS, no earcons beyond the bell, no humanized tool names, no heading discipline in model output (Anthropic confirmed these are unshipped, Aug 17, 2026); attached background sessions enter the alternate screen (#100922, Oct 9, 2026); slash-command menu arrow keys write nothing in SR mode (#100253, Oct 7, 2026); VoiceOver still hits runs of box-drawing chars (#91058, Aug 31, 2026).

in_window.name: Claude Code CLI screen reader mode (--ax-screen-reader)
in_window.category: screen-reader-friendly agent CLI
in_window.what_it_does: Opt-in plain, linear text rendering of the Claude Code terminal UI: no box-drawing or redraws, labeled transcript lines (you:, claude:, thinking:, tool:, Permission Required:, Cost:), numbered menus answered by typing a number, y/n prompts, diffs read line by line with +/-, tables as 'Header: value' sentences, a terminal bell when Claude finishes/needs input/long tool ends, OSC 133 markers for jump-to-previous-turn, spoken deleted-text announcements, permission-mode announcements on Shift+Tab. Enabled via flag, CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1, or axScreenReader:true; tuning via CLAUDE_AX_STARTUP_QUIET_MS and CLAUDE_AX_PREPARK_MS; separate CLAUDE_CODE_ACCESSIBILITY=1 keeps a native cursor for magnifiers; prefersReducedMotion; daltonized themes.
in_window.date_or_version: Announced Jul 1, 2026 as available in v2.1.181 (collaborator georgez-a11y, 'not officially released yet'); 'properly released' with docs Jul 20, 2026; changelog entries continue through v2.1.296 (2.1.200 glyph hiding, 2.1.208 'Added screen reader mode' entry, 2.1.210 permission-mode announcements, 2.1.217/218/219/222 input-echo fixes, 2.1.233 /effort numbered list, 2.1.282/283/288 fixes, 2.1.296 reduced-motion fix). Window-verified.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: This is the tool blind developers in the issues say moved them from 'nearly unusable' to daily CLI use; it is the de-facto reference design other projects (OpenCode requests, BlindPilot, earshot) copy. It is how a blind person can drive a full coding agent end to end from a terminal today.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Labeled, searchable transcript prefixes; numbered-list menus + typed-number selection; y/n typed answers; diff narration before approval; bell on turn end; OSC 133 turn markers; echo-only-changed-characters typing; announcing deleted text; quiet period after startup line; flag > env > setting precedence; a documented 'Known limitations' list.
in_window.gaps_left_open: Not auto-enabled when a screen reader is detected (#89002); slash-command menu arrows write nothing in SR mode (#100253, Oct 7, 2026); AskUserQuestion picker unusable with NVDA (#88839); some options truncated in manual mode (#99660); no built-in TTS/earcons/humanized tool names (staff confirmed not shipped, Aug 17, 2026); no 'hold speech until turn done' option (#87978); text-selection not announced (#92287); desktop app virtualized transcript unmounts what JAWS is reading (#99332) and NVDA not announcing replies (#95937).

in_window.name: AI Content Describer for NVDA 2026.05.06 (adds fully local 'Seer' descriptions)

in_window.date_or_version: Version 2026.05.06 released May 6, 2026 (the only release in window; previous Jun 17, 2025). Window-verified.

in_window.name: BlindPilot (screen-reader-first desktop app for coding agents) and its origin Claude Code Reader
in_window.category: accessible agent frontend built by a blind developer
in_window.what_it_does: wxPython native-widget desktop app that runs Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, opencode, Antigravity CLI, Hermes, FreeBuff, Muse Code, muse.ai, Command Code, or direct API chat; splits each answer into arrow-navigable rows (headings, paragraphs, code, tool steps), narration modes ('Follow everything'/'Keep up'), permission and multiple-choice dialogs, subagent viewer, sound cues per backend, Linux announcements via off-screen GTK accessible for Orca, plan-limit/context warnings, self-update with SHA-256. 'Every agent runs in Bypass permissions mode out of the box.' Origin: Claude Code Reader (created May 5, 2026, 'tested with VoiceOver... NVDA and JAWS').
in_window.date_or_version: v0.3.0 Aug 9, 2026 through v0.43.3 Oct 11, 2026 (CHANGELOG dates; ~43 tagged versions); 11 stars, 523 commits. Window-verified.
in_window.relevance_to_blind_creators: The clearest existing answer to 'how does a blind person vibe-code with many agents': a native-widget wrapper, written by a blind dev who 'uses it every day', that sidesteps terminals entirely.
in_window.features_worth_borrowing: Answer-as-list navigation; per-backend earcons; 'Keep up' narration that skips to latest; explicit stop/redirect of a running task; subagent view; warnings read aloud once; wizard that installs and signs into agents.
in_window.gaps_left_open: Defaults to bypass-permissions (risky); macOS build not notarized, Linux least tested; single maintainer; no automated screen-reader tests.

verification.name: BlindPilot (screen-reader-first desktop app for coding agents) and its origin Claude Code Reader
verification.corrected_description: BlindPilot (serrebidev, MIT, 11 stars, created 2026-08-09) is a wxPython native-widget desktop frontend for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, opencode, Hermes, FreeBuff, Muse Code, muse.ai and Command Code plus API chat, forked from doubletaponair/claude-code-reader (created 2026-05-05). CHANGELOG runs from 0.3.0 (2026-08-09) to 0.43.3 (2026-10-11) with over 130 tagged versions, not ~43. Features confirmed: 'Follow everything'/'Keep up' narration, subagent viewer, sound cues, Linux announcements to Orca via off-screen GTK accessible (0.7.0), SHA-256-verified updater and Node download, context/plan-limit warnings, 'Every agent runs in Bypass permissions mode out of the box', unnotarized macOS build, Linux least tested. The README says the author uses it daily and it was vibe-coded, but does not state the author is blind. Claude Code Reader's README says it was tested with VoiceOver and with the Win32 accessibility APIs that NVDA and JAWS use, not that it was tested directly with NVDA and JAWS.
verification.corrected_date: BlindPilot v0.3.0 2026-08-09 through v0.43.3 2026-10-11; Claude Code Reader created 2026-05-05 (last push 2026-06-14)
verification.verdict_reason: GitHub API search confirms repo metadata (created 2026-08-09, pushed 2026-10-11, 11 stars, Python, MIT) and the origin repo (created 2026-05-05, 4 stars). Tag commit dates confirm v0.3.0 on 2026-08-09 and v0.43.3 on 2026-10-11; git ls-remote shows 133 tags. README and CHANGELOG confirm nearly every listed feature. Two overstatements: the scout's 'blind dev who uses it every day' is only half-supported (daily use is stated, blindness is not), and the origin's NVDA/JAWS testing claim is indirect.

background.name: Cursor IDE (AI editor) screen-reader status
background.what_it_does: Cursor inherits VS Code's editor accessibility (works with ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED=1 per an April 2026 forum reply) but community reports through May 2026 say the AI chat/agent dialogue, 'generate' input in edit mode, chat focus loss, and approval/submit buttons remain inaccessible or keyboard-unreachable with NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver. No official Cursor accessibility release or roadmap was found.
background.date_or_version: Forum threads active April-May 2026; no dated vendor fix found.
background.relevance_to_blind_creators: CREATE (negative finding): the most popular GUI AI editor is effectively unusable for the agent part; blind creators gravitate to terminal agents (Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Codex) instead. No evidence found on Lovable, Bolt, Replit or v0 accessibility.
background.features_worth_borrowing: None observed; the gap itself is the lesson - agent chat panels need ARIA live regions, headings, reachable approve/submit controls.
background.gaps_left_open: Agent dialogue 'completely opaque'; no official response; blind teams rejected it.

verification.name: Cursor IDE (AI editor) screen-reader status
verification.corrected_description: The three Cursor forum threads exist and say what the scout reports: the 'generate' input is blank to NVDA once in edit mode; a blind user says AI suggestions can't be read and the agent dialogue is 'completely opaque' with NVDA/JAWS, while a reply notes the editor itself works with ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED=1 (upstream VS Code); a VoiceOver/macOS report praises editor accessibility but lists text-selection and Fast Search failures; further threads cover chat-panel focus loss and inaccessible approval/submit buttons. No official Cursor accessibility statement or fix was found. However, thread dates could not be confirmed: threads 26110 and 56823 have low IDs and almost certainly predate April 2026, so the 'April-May 2026 activity' is unverified and this is an ongoing gap rather than an in-window event.
verification.corrected_date: Undated; forum threads likely span 2024-2026, in-window activity unconfirmed
verification.verdict_reason: Search confirmed the forum threads and their content, but no dated in-window post or vendor response could be verified, so in_window is set false conservatively.

background.name: Neural and Behavioral Correlates of Evidence Accumulation in Human Click-Based Echolocation
background.category: Neuroscience paper — blind expert echolocators' perceptual strength (eNeuro)
background.maker: Haydee García-Lázaro, Santani Teng (Smith-Kettlewell Eye Research Institute)
background.what_it_does: Blind expert echolocators (n=4) and sighted novices (n=21) localized virtual spatialized echoes from synthesized mouth clicks in trains of 2–11 clicks, with EEG. Experts significantly outperformed sighted controls and their accuracy improved as more clicks were presented, consistent with cumulative integration of spatial information; EEG decoding accuracy and variability across clicks tracked perceptual performance (effect seen in some experts, not uniformly).
background.date_or_version: eNeuro, published online 6 April 2026, DOI 10.1523/ENEURO.0342-25.2026 — NOTE: six days BEFORE the 12 April window start; bioRxiv preprint Aug 2025. Included as the key 2026 cognitive-strength study, with the date caveat.
background.relevance_to_blind_creators: Empirical support for the 'blind people perceive things sighted people don't' premise: expert blind echolocators actively accumulate spatial evidence over repeated self-generated sounds. Suggests interface designs that let blind users 're-ping' (re-query) and integrate repeated audio probes rather than one-shot descriptions.
background.features_worth_borrowing: Iterative probing as an interaction primitive; spatialized audio cues; trust that expert blind users can integrate many short audio samples quickly.
background.gaps_left_open: n=4 experts; lab task; not about tools or building.

verification.name: Grid-Coding: An Accessible, Efficient, and Structured Coding Paradigm for Blind and Low-Vision Programmers
verification.corrected_description: Real paper, but it is a UIST 2022 paper, not UIST 2026. Authors: Md Ehtesham-Ul-Haque, Syed Mostofa Monsur and Syed Masum Billah (Penn State A11y Lab), UIST '22 Article 44, DOI 10.1145/3526113.3545620, Best Paper Award at UIST 2022. It renders Python source in a spreadsheet-like 2D grid with consistent row/column/cell semantics; a study with 12 BLV programmers showed faster navigation, easier context finding and fewer syntax errors versus a text editor. The conference-aggregator page that listed it under 'UIST 2026' appears to have reused old best-paper data. No UIST 2026 follow-up was found, and the 'pairing with LLM agents for cell-level editing' feature attributed by the scout is not part of this paper.
verification.corrected_date: UIST 2022 (October/November 2022)
verification.verdict_reason: Paper exists and did win a UIST best paper award, but in 2022; the scout's UIST 2026 attribution came from an aggregator and is wrong. Outside the window.
